title: They Won the World Cup Ten Days Ago. Now India's Women Are in England for a Three-Match T20I Series That Starts Thursday.
excerpt: Fresh from their ODI World Cup triumph, Harmanpreet Kaur's squad plays England at Chelmsford on May 28 — the first of three T20Is across three English counties. For NRIs in the UK, this is the most accessible Indian cricket of the year.
body:
India's women won the ODI World Cup in spectacular fashion. The celebrations have barely faded. And now, less than a fortnight later, the squad has flown to England for a three-match T20 International series that begins on Thursday at the County Cricket Ground in Chelmsford.

The Schedule

The series runs from May 28 to June 2, with each match at a different venue across England's county circuit:

  • 1st T20I — May 28, Chelmsford (County Cricket Ground, Essex)
  • 2nd T20I — May 30, Bristol (County Ground, Gloucestershire)
  • 3rd T20I — June 2, Taunton (Cooper Associates County Ground, Somerset)

All three matches start at 5:30 PM local time (10:00 PM IST, 12:30 PM Eastern, 9:30 AM Pacific).

The Squad

India are carrying the same core group that won the World Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur leads, with Smriti Mandhana as vice-captain. The batting order that dismantled opponents in the 50-over format — Shefali Verma at the top, Jemimah Rodrigues in the middle, Richa Ghosh keeping wicket — remains intact.

Deepti Sharma and Sneh Rana provide the spin depth. Arundhati Reddy leads the pace attack. Yastika Bhatia offers flexibility, and Amanjot Kaur's all-round abilities give Harmanpreet options.

England, playing at home, have named a strong squad led by Heather Knight. Sophie Ecclestone, the world's top-ranked T20I bowler, anchors their spin attack. Amy Jones keeps wicket. Danielle Wyatt-Hodge and Sophia Dunkley add firepower to the top order. Lauren Filer and Issy Wong lead the pace department. Alice Capsey's all-round talent gives England depth through the middle overs.

The Context

This bilateral series sits between two major ICC events. India have just won the ODI World Cup. In late June, the T20 World Cup begins — also in England, with matches at Edgbaston, Lord's, and other iconic venues. This three-match series is both a reward for the World Cup winners and a preparation block for what comes next.

For Harmanpreet, the series offers a chance to fine-tune T20-specific combinations. The powerplay approach in T20 cricket demands a different rhythm than the measured ODI game. Shefali Verma's aggressive opening, Jemimah's ability to rotate strike in the middle overs, and Richa Ghosh's finishing — all need recalibration for the shorter format.

England, for their part, will be desperate to reassert themselves. They were knocked out of the ODI World Cup earlier than expected. Home conditions and home crowds could help restore confidence before the T20 World Cup on their own soil.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

This is the most accessible live Indian cricket for NRIs in the UK this year. Chelmsford, Bristol, and Taunton are within easy reach of London, Birmingham, and the wider South West. County grounds are intimate. Tickets are affordable. The atmosphere at a women's international in England — vocal, family-friendly, and increasingly packed — is entirely different from the corporate feel of a Lord's Test.

For the Indian diaspora in Essex, the Chelmsford match on Thursday is essentially a home game. The county has one of the largest South Asian populations outside London. Bristol and Taunton, while smaller, have growing Indian communities and are popular weekend destinations.

The women's game has seen a surge in attendance across England in recent years. The Hundred, county T20s, and international fixtures regularly draw strong South Asian crowds. This series should be no exception.

What to Watch For

Smriti Mandhana's form. The left-hander was imperious in the World Cup. In T20Is, she's even more dangerous — her strike rate climbs, her shot selection sharpens. England's bowlers will test her early with the swinging ball.

Sophie Ecclestone vs India's right-handers. The left-arm spinner is the world's best in this format. How India's middle order handles her through the powerplay and middle overs will shape the series. Jemimah Rodrigues, who sweeps well, could be the key matchup.

Shefali Verma's evolution. At twenty-two, she's no longer a prodigy. She's an established international opener. Her ability to dominate the first six overs sets the template for India's innings. English conditions — lateral movement, variable bounce — will test her technique against pace.

Richa Ghosh's finishing. The wicketkeeper-batter has become India's most reliable death-overs player. In English conditions — where the ball might swing late and boundaries are shorter — she could be decisive in tight chases.

Deepti Sharma's all-round value. She bats, she bowls off-spin, she fields at slip. In English conditions where spin might grip on county pitches, her role could be elevated beyond what she was required to do in the World Cup.

How to Watch

In India, the series will be available on Star Sports and JioHotstar. In the UK, Sky Sports Cricket has the rights. In the US and Canada, Willow TV carries Indian women's cricket. The first ball at Chelmsford is at 5:30 PM BST on Thursday, May 28.

The World Cup was the headline. This series is the fine print. And in cricket, the fine print is where matches are won.
